# Maintained connection-task ownership hook

This is the published reqwest 0.12.28 archive from crates.io, SHA-256
`eddd3ca559203180a307f12d114c268abf583f59b03cb906fd0b3ff8646c1147`.
The upstream MIT and Apache-2.0 license files are retained.

The patch adds optional `ClientBuilder::connection_task_executor` and its small
`ConnectionTaskExecutor` interface. It substitutes that executor at the existing
hyper-util client builder. Without the option, the original Tokio executor is
used. The interface carries caller admission through destruction of actual
HTTP connection tasks, including the HTTP/1 dispatcher that survives request
cancellation. It does not replace request construction, HTTP, DNS, TLS, or
certificate verification.

Positron's Google native transport uses the hook for HTTPS and pinned metadata
HTTP clients. It bounds detached connection tasks separately from request
futures, records refusal as a typed resource-capacity failure, and holds the
original governor grant until task destruction. HTTP/1 and disabled idle
pooling bound the tasks generated by this client. The existing AWS client does
not select the new hook.

Only `src/async_impl/client.rs`, `src/async_impl/mod.rs` and `src/lib.rs` differ
from the published source, plus this provenance document. The package is
excluded from workspace membership and selected through the root Cargo patch.
